item.title: More on the Fed’s New Game of Monetary Policy Football
item.description: Revisiting the Maradona theory of interest rates.

item.title: SpaceX Short Interest Soars Ahead of Big Share Unlock, Earnings
item.description: Short sellers have piled into SpaceX at a rapid pace ahead of two major milestones next week: the company’s first earnings report as a public company and the release of hundreds of millions of locked-up shares.

item.title: Inside Tencent’s Failed Attempt to Take On ‘Grand Theft Auto’
item.description: Lightspeed’s Last Sentinel burnt through six years of development and hundreds of millions of dollars

item.title: Eric Trump Expands Family’s Defense Portfolio With Space-Eyes
item.description: Defense software company Space-Eyes enlisted Eric Trump as an investor and adviser, expanding the first family’s military technology portfolio amid criticism from ethics watchdogs and President Donald Trump’s political opponents.

item.title: How Is Student Debt Impacting Your Finances? Share Your Story
item.description: After President Donald Trump ended a yearslong pause on student loan collections, default rates are at historic highs. How is education debt squeezing your finances and influencing your vote?

item.title: Muni Market Has Worst July Since 2003, Veering From Typical Summer Pattern
item.description: US state and local government debt is on track to notch its weakest July in more than two decades, as rising benchmark Treasury yields and a flood of new issuance take a toll on what usually is one of the strongest months for the $4 trillion market.

item.title: Index Ventures, Firm Behind Wiz, Revolut, Raises $2 Billion for Trio of Funds
item.description: Index Ventures, an investor in cybersecurity firm Wiz and fintech Revolut, has raised $2 billion in new capital to back startups across multiple stages of development.

item.title: Costs to Hedge Against a Deeper Selloff in US Bonds Are Soaring
item.description: Bond traders are paying the highest premiums since March to protect against a further climb in longer-dated yields, as the fallout from this week’s Federal Reserve policy meeting continues to ripple through the rates market.

item.title: Cable One Creditors Organize, Pressuring Plans for New Capital
item.description: Cable One Inc. creditors have begun mobilizing in different groups as a steep selloff in the broadband company’s debt complicates its plans for fresh capital.

item.title: US Treasury Weighs Repo Entry That Could Reshape Funding Markets
item.description: The US Treasury is exploring bringing some of its cash pile into the roughly $13 trillion market for repurchase agreements, reviving a two-decade old idea and sparking a debate around its potential to reshape a key part of the financial system’s plumbing.

item.title: Treasuries Fall as Fed Dissenters Flag Risks, Oil Prices Climb
item.description: Treasuries fell after Federal Reserve policymakers who dissented from this week’s decision not to raise interest rates said hikes were needed to tame inflation, and as oil prices climbed.

item.title: Chile Posts Weakest Copper Output for Second Quarter in 19 Years
item.description: Chile registered its weakest second quarter of copper production in data going back to 2007, underscoring the challenge facing the world’s biggest supplier as aging mines struggle to lift output despite billions of dollars of investment.

item.title: Jane Street-Backed Exchange Sells Control to TMX Group
item.description: MEMX LLC, an exchange operator backed by Jane Street and Morgan Stanley, will combine with equity options market BOX in a deal that gives control of the merged entity to Canada’s leading stock exchange group.

item.title: US Backing of Japan Yen Actions Marks New Normal in Coordination
item.description: Cooperation between the US and Japan to buttress a flailing yen appears to be tightening to a degree unseen in decades, with the two sides jointly pushing back against moves in the $9.5 trillion-a-day global foreign exchange market.

item.title: Proto Labs Lifts Guidance on New Data Center, Defense Clients
item.description: Automated manufacturing company Proto Labs Inc. raised its full-year outlook after earnings reached a seven-year high, helped by renewed strength in its injection molding business and new data center and defense customers.

item.title: Federal Reserve Unveils Plan Aiming to Boost Mutual Bank Growth
item.description: Mutual banks would see more “flexibility” for raising capital under a plan unveiled by the Federal Reserve on Friday.

item.title: Bank of England Hawks Appear Isolated as Deputies Shift Ground
item.description: Clear blue water is emerging on the Bank of England’s rate-setting committee with its three hawks now looking increasingly stranded in their push for higher interest rates.

item.title: UK Chancellor John Healey to Deliver First Budget on October 28
item.description: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will deliver his first budget on Oct. 28, a key moment for Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s new administration.

item.title: Jana Adds More Sale Pressure on Alkami in New Letter to Board
item.description: Activist investor Jana Parners contends Alkami Technology Inc. is failing to run a true sale process, according to a new letter to the fintech company’s board that was reviewed by Bloomberg News.

item.title: US Consumer Sentiment Rises to a Five-Month High in July
item.description: US consumer sentiment rose to five-month high in July as views about the outlook improved and gasoline prices remained below war-time highs.

item.title: Exxon, Chevron Steer Windfall Profits Into Paying Down Debt
item.description: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. and Chevron Corp. plowed blowout profits into debt reduction rather than huge buyback increases in a sign of Big Oil’s caution about how long war-driven price rallies will last.

item.title: BOE’s Pill Warns of Energy Price Volatility Persisting Into 2027
item.description: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said the wild swings in energy and commodity prices due to the Iran war could linger into 2027, highlighting the risk that inflation stays elevated for longer and forces policymakers to respond

item.title: As NYSE, Nasdaq, LSE Head For Nonstop Trading, Can Traders Handle It? Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about the rise of nonstop trading and what it means for markets in a Live Q&A on Tuesday, August 4 at 2 p.m. BST.

item.title: Brazil Market Open Delayed as B3 Sees Processing Issues
item.description: Trading in most Brazil assets was suspended on Friday as the country’s main stock exchange was hit by technical issues in a halt that was set to almost halve the local market session.

item.title: US Employment Costs Grew at a Steady Pace in Second Quarter
item.description: US labor cost growth remained steady in the second quarter, indicating the job market is doing little to contribute to inflationary pressures.

item.title: Canada Economy Tracking 3.4% Second Quarter Annualized Growth
item.description: The Canadian economy is on track for a stronger-than-expected rebound in the second quarter, as oil and gas led growth in May for a second consecutive month.

item.title: India Monsoon Set to Extend Weak Run Straining Farms and Power
item.description: India’s vital monsoon season is forecast to deliver below-normal rainfall through the rest of the season, deepening the stress on crops and power supplies, and adding to inflation risks.

item.title: Moonshot’s Kimi Built on 20,000 Nvidia Chip Cluster From Alibaba
item.description: Chinese AI champion Moonshot has a computing power agreement with Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. for the use of around 20,000 Nvidia Corp. chips, underscoring China’s continued reliance on Western semiconductors to fuel its AI development, according to people with knowledge of the companies’ operations.

item.title: Traders Gird for More S&P 500 Volatility as Marco Risks Rise
item.description: For months, the S&P 500 Index has remained idle, despite stomach-churning swings in individual sectors that largely canceled each other out. But traders are positioning for the setup to start changing soon.

item.title: Texas Stock Exchange Heralds Debut With Sights on NYSE, Nasdaq
item.description: The Texas Stock Exchange has rolled out trading for all tickers as the upstart venue steps up its drive to win business from Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange.
